//: Historial de versiones en inglés: una entrada por cada «- X.Y.Z (fecha): texto» del docstring de version.py, que es el original en español. Otro idioma = otro archivo <idioma>.json en esta carpeta. Ver services/auto_update.py.
3.2.6: Pregeneration also shows on the Server page: with the server running and Chunky installed, a card shows the progress (percentage, chunks, speed and time left) and updates by itself, without switching tabs. Without Chunky it doesn't appear.
3.2.5: Pregeneration fix. If you install Chunky while the server is running, the panel warns that it won't work until you restart it and the task waits for that restart, instead of sending the console commands Minecraft doesn't know yet. A pregeneration left half-way like that starts again by itself after the restart instead of getting stuck.
3.2.4: The Pregenerate button moves to each server's header, next to Player pack, and can be seen from any tab (it used to be tucked away in Properties, next to the installed worlds).
3.2.3: A tidy-up of the interface under the hood. If a configuration file no longer exists, the editor says so instead of opening it with "undefined" inside (and that text can no longer be saved over it); a failure while looking for duplicate or client-only mods no longer shows up as "all good", nor one while syncing players as "Synced". Screen readers announce the title of every dialog and the name of the search boxes and filters. The CSS is organised by section, with no visible changes.
3.2.2: Fixes. On the login screen, the password you're typing (and the error message) no longer clears itself every 30 seconds. The config, KubeJS and world file lists now show what the server creates in subfolders (e.g. a new player's stats) without restarting the panel. A damaged compressed log says it's damaged and can be downloaded, instead of giving an error.
3.2.1: The panel’s code is now under the MIT licence (LICENSE file): free software anyone can use, modify and share. No changes to how it works.
3.2.0: Pregenerate the world with Chunky, from Properties. The panel only installs it if you ask (and keeps it out of the player pack), tells you beforehand how much space it’ll take based on your own world, won’t start if it doesn’t fit on the disk, can pause while players are online and carries on by itself after a restart. Servers created from scratch no longer accept the EULA on their own either.
3.1.9: The app is now called “Server Deployer for Minecraft”. The Minecraft EULA is no longer accepted automatically: the first time you start each server the panel shows it to you and you accept it (it’s recorded in Activity). The player pack’s .mrpack no longer includes mods whose author doesn’t allow them to be shared outside CurseForge. New “Legal notice” section in Help.
3.1.8: “Player pack” (in the modpack header, and in the Server header while it's running): the server's modpack ready to install on your computer with the same mods and versions, as CurseForge (.zip) or Modrinth (.mrpack). If the server is linked to its original modpack, it also includes its client-only mods, resource packs, shaders and configs. Limited accounts can download it too.
3.1.7: under the hood: the CurseForge fingerprint used to recognise mods is computed in a single place, and the missing-dependency search computes it somewhat faster. No changes for you.
3.1.6: under the hood: automated tests now run on GitHub every time a change is published (with Python 3.10 and 3.14), no changes for you.
3.1.5: more automated tests: reading mods (Fabric, NeoForge, Quilt), compatible versions, duplicates, crash analysis, console parsing and that no panel route can escape the server folder. Fixed: crash analysis now also points to mods whose Java package has underscores.
3.1.4: internals: modpack installation has been split into smaller modules (Modrinth, CurseForge, shared pieces and the duplicate warning), with no changes for you. Wording: «añadir» instead of «agregar» in the Spanish texts.
3.1.3: “When people play” on the Players page: streak of days in a row with someone playing, a summary of the last 7 days and a heatmap by day and hour. On Mondays the weekly summary arrives by Telegram or Discord. New achievement: “On a roll”.
3.1.2: limited accounts: they can see everything, but can only start, stop and restart the server and manage the whitelist (no mods, worlds, backups, console, downloads or RCON password). Chosen when creating the account or from the Users list, and the change applies straight away. Fixed: non-administrator accounts no longer get an error when viewing the firewall status.
3.1.1: scheduled restarts and stops can run only when nobody is online (if people are, they wait for them to leave, up to the maximum you choose), and the server can stop itself after being empty for a while. Fixed: the task form showed fields that didn't apply (Command, Which server).
3.1.0: activity log on the Users page (administrator only): who did what and when, with their IP (starting and stopping, console commands, mods, backups, settings changes, logins and failed attempts), and what the panel does on its own, like automatic backups or restarts after a crash. It can be filtered by person and type.
3.0.9: «Update modpack» button when managing a server: moves it to another version of its Modrinth or CurseForge modpack after a full backup, without touching the world, server.properties or the player lists, and keeping the mods you added. It keeps going on the server even if the browser is closed. Servers installed earlier are linked to their modpack by searching for it once. New achievement: New season.
3.0.8: «Check for updates» button in the Mods tab: recognises each mod by its hash on Modrinth (and on CurseForge if there's an API key), shows the ones with a newer version for your Minecraft version and modloader (never going from stable to beta) and updates the ones you pick, checking the download. The old files are kept and «Undo» puts them back. New achievement: Tune-up.
3.0.7: optional two-step verification for each account (padlock button → Set up): logging in also asks for a 6-digit code from a phone app, with 8 recovery codes in case it's lost. The administrator can remove it from another account in Users, and their own with set_password.py. Also, the lock after several failed attempts is no longer cleared when the panel restarts. New achievement: Double lock.
3.0.6: full backups and a secondary destination. In Modpacks → Backups, besides the world backup there's a «Full backup» with mods, config, scripts and player lists: restoring it leaves the server exactly as it was (it can also be chosen for automatic backups). In Automation you can choose a secondary destination (another disk, a NAS) where every backup is duplicated; if the one on the main disk is lost, it's restored from there. A backup that won't fit on the disk is no longer started, and the panel warns when space is running low. New achievement: Time capsule.
3.0.5: app updates undo themselves if they go wrong: before restarting, the panel checks that the new version loads (and installs its new libraries if needed), and if it then fails to start or respond, it goes back to the previous version on its own and says so in System → Updates. It also won't update if any of the app's files were changed by hand.
3.0.4: Spanish review: removed the remaining Latin American expressions from texts, comments, installers and docs (e.g. «Último chequeo» is now «Última comprobación»).
3.0.3: achievements belong to your account, not your browser: they're the same on every device you log in from. Any you already had in a browser are uploaded to your account the first time you log in with it.
3.0.2: what's new in each version (System → Updates) is shown in each account's language. The translations go in one file per language, static/i18n/changelog/<language>.json.
3.0.1: the descriptions in Settings → Constants and their validation error are now in English too.
3.0.0: translations finished: the whole panel in English, each account with its own language and the notifications language chosen by the administrator. The installers (install.sh and setup.py) ask for the language first, and the README has an English version.
2.2.7: achievements and login screen phrases in English too, and decimal numbers use a comma in Spanish (1,5 GB).
2.2.6: server errors and messages come in each account's language, installation progress included. In Settings → Notifications you choose the language of the Telegram and Discord messages.
2.2.5: each account has its own language. It applies on login, from any device, and when you log out the login screen goes back to the default language.
2.2.4: everything about managing modpacks is now in English too: mods, search and install, dependencies, worlds, logs, KubeJS, RAM, modloader and the file editor.
2.2.3: the messages that appear while using the panel are now in English too: notices, confirmations, server states, System, Players, Backups, Automation, Users and Settings. Dates, weekdays and numbers follow the chosen language. Modpack management will come in the next version.
2.2.2: all the panel's fixed text is now in English if you choose it: pages, tabs, forms, dialogs and Help. The messages that appear while using the panel (notices, states, lists) will come in the next version.
2.2.1: first step towards an English panel. The language is chosen in Appearance (also from the login screen) and the default language in Settings. For now the login screen, the menu and Appearance are translated; the rest will come in the next versions.
2.2.0: secrets never go out to the browser anymore. JWT_SECRET, the CurseForge API key, the Telegram token and the Discord webhook show up as “Saved”: leaving them empty keeps the current one, typing a new one changes it and the “Remove” button deletes it.
2.1.9: the panel looks right on mobile: Logs puts the list above the viewer, the Mods search box gets its own row, the Install disk bar no longer disappears, the Players title isn't squashed and the eye button is easier to tap. JWT_SECRET and the CurseForge API key are hidden in Settings (with the eye to show them). Also: ellipses and «» quotes in the texts, and a single theme colour for shadows.
2.1.8: before updating, System → Updates shows what the new version brings: the changes of each pending version (taken from this history) and, by their subject, the commits that have no entry.
2.1.7: smoother animations (progress bars, toggles and the scene's sun/moon move with transform, not width/left), icons hidden from screen readers, buttons sink 1px when pressed and nothing overflows sideways (overflow-x: clip, no 100vw).
2.1.6: animated feedback: the missing field shakes and gets highlighted (no modal dialog), whatever was just added flashes in its list and save buttons confirm with “Saved”.
2.1.5: loading state on every button that waits for the server (spinner, no double click): players, worlds, mods, KubeJS, editor, server.properties, users, backups, tasks and Force stop.
2.1.4: balanced line breaks in titles and centred text (text-wrap: balance) and no orphan words in paragraphs and hints (text-wrap: pretty).
2.1.3: tabular figures across the panel; the metrics (TPS, MSPT, players, RAM) no longer change width when counting in the block font.
2.1.2: AA contrast (4.5:1) in every theme: dark text on the coloured dialog buttons and the red badge, log line numbers, task weekdays, the red of danger buttons and Minecraft colours §0/§1/§4/§5/§8/§9.
2.1.1: concentric corners (inner radius = outer - padding) in segmented controls, the network toggle, the Mods menu, dropdown lists, the mobile menu drawer and theme swatches.
2.1.0: the console prompt in chat mode uses the Chat tab icon instead of the 💬 emoji.
2.0.9: consistent icons: every toolbar and row action has an icon (worlds, users, KubeJS, modloader, Force stop) and “Install server” uses the same icon as its “Upload a modpack” tab.
2.0.8: the final Install button (upload, create or download) stands out more: bigger, with an icon and a green glow once it can be pressed.
2.0.7: removed repeated labels (aria-label equal to the text and repeated tooltips in the menu, and the “More options” tooltip in Mods).
2.0.6: removed filler badges in the mod search (“Stable”, “Latest” and the “Installed” repeated next to the check mark).
2.0.5: removed pagination from lists that already scrolled (mod config, KubeJS, world files, mod dialogs and a mod's versions): they're shown in full, with the total underneath.
2.0.4: instead of merging them, the statistics only show the ones for the current online-mode (offline or premium UUID).
2.0.3: the statistics merge the same player when online-mode was changed after the world had been played (they showed up twice, once per UUID).
2.0.2: the Server page metrics refresh every 10 s with freshly requested data and the Performance charts every minute.
2.0.1: ops, whitelist and bans adapt to the current online-mode on startup (changing it after installing left players without op). Also includes that day's unnumbered work: seeing a modpack's mods before installing it, lists taken from the CurseForge Server Pack, ServerPackCreator's variables.txt respected and scripts stuck on “Press any key”.
2.0.0: security review (RAM validated on every path, private .env/users.json, upload limits, login lockout per IP, atomic writes, CSP), changing your own password and resetting other users' passwords.
